subject: GA Go/No-Go: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode (Sep 3)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: GA Go/No-Go: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode (Sep 3)
Attachments: Dedicated-Autoscaling-Bounds_GA-GoNoGo-Checklist_v3.pdf, Dedicated-Autoscaling-Bounds_GA-Launch-Brief_2025-09-03.docx

Priya,

Requesting GA go/no-go today for Dedicated autoscaling bounds (min/max) + predictive mode (opt-in).

Current status summary (details in attached checklist):

1) Engineering
- Min/max bounds enforcement: COMPLETE (rolled to canary + 3 pilots)
- Predictive mode: COMPLETE (opt-in, staleness checks, reactive fallback)
- Anti-oscillation: COMPLETE (cooldowns + dampening)
- Audit events: COMPLETE (policy changes + scaling decisions w/ reasons)

2) Operability
- Dashboards: COMPLETE
- Alerts: COMPLETE (max-bound saturation + sustained queue depth)
- Runbook: COMPLETE (autoscaler troubleshooting + mitigations)

3) Customer-facing
- Docs: READY (PR merged / publishing queued)
- Release notes: READY
- CS enablement: READY (support macros + escalation path)

4) Open issues / risks
- Capacity shortage behavior when min bound cannot be met: implemented + alerts; want final sign-off on messaging (“degraded” state) before broad enablement
- Pilot incident last month (oscillation + null predictor output): hotfix shipped; no recurrence in the last 10 days

Proposed GA scope:
- Bounds: GA for all Dedicated accounts (behind account-level flag default ON for new Dedicated; existing accounts remain unchanged until enabled)
- Predictive: GA as “beta within GA” (flagged, opt-in per deployment)

If you’re ok, we’ll proceed with GA announcement in the internal changelog and enablement in Console next week.

Thanks,
Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product Lead, Dedicated
Redwood Inference


From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 3, 2025 at 10:04 AM PDT
Subject: Re: GA Go/No-Go: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode (Sep 3)

+1 from Infra on GA for bounds.

A few concrete datapoints from canary + pilots (us-west-2 only):
- Bound clamping is deterministic and we’re logging both requested_desired + bounded_desired w/ reason.
- Bound-hit metric is clean (no weird spikes outside expected traffic ramps).
- The null predictor issue is fully addressed (PR-48321). We also added an additional guard in the autoscaler loop so “missing forecast” can’t reduce desired below reactive recommendation.

Remaining watch item:
- Region shortage + unmet min: we surface “min_unmet” in the deployment status and alert on it. Behavior is: keep retrying w/ backoff; do not steal capacity across tenants.

I’m comfortable with GA under the staged enablement Lauren outlined (existing customers opt-in).

Vanessa

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Fleet Autoscaling Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 3, 2025 at 11:16 AM PDT
Subject: Re: GA Go/No-Go: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode (Sep 3)

I’m ok to GA bounds with the constraint that:

1) We do not silently change behavior for existing Dedicated deployments.
2) We keep guardrails on “high min” settings. If a customer config implies a min that materially changes our reserved capacity planning (e.g., >X GPUs / region), it needs manual approval until we’ve seen a quarter of data.
3) We ship with clear customer comms for “min not met due to region capacity shortage” (degraded state + what we’ll do + what customer can do).

On SRE readiness: my understanding is the runbook + alerts were exercised during the last game day and looked reasonable (noise acceptable). I don’t need a separate meeting if Priya is satisfied with the attached checklist.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
VP Infrastructure & Reliability
Redwood Inference


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 3, 2025 at 12:02 PM PDT
Subject: Re: GA Go/No-Go: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode (Sep 3)

Thanks—aligned on the constraints.

Customer comms/doc status:
- Dedicated docs: updated with semantics (bounds precedence, “hard” enforcement, predictive opt-in) + guidance on choosing min/max. Publishing is queued today.
- “Min unmet due to shortage” is explicitly called out as a possible degraded state, with recommended actions.
- CS playbook includes: questions to ask, how to interpret bounded metrics, and the escalation criteria.

Enablement plan:
- Existing Dedicated: no changes until a CSM/Support request and internal approval (we’ll continue using INT-9412-style helpdesk request).
- New Dedicated: bounds UI visible, but default values preserve current behavior unless customer edits (min unset; max unset).
- Predictive: remains opt-in behind feature flag (per deployment), and we’ll keep “reactive overrides prediction” semantics.

If helpful I can also paste the GA checklist section on rollback:
- Disable predictive flag (per deployment or per account) -> immediate revert to reactive-only.
- Bounds stay enforced (cannot exceed max / drop below min); if we need to revert enforcement globally, it’s a single config kill-switch in autoscaler (documented in runbook).

Lauren


From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 3, 2025 at 1:10 PM PDT
Subject: Re: GA Go/No-Go: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode (Sep 3)

A couple final questions before I approve:

1) Alerts: do we have a clear paging threshold for “max bound saturation + queue buildup” that won’t page on normal ramps?
2) Auditability: can we answer “who changed the bounds and what did it do” for an enterprise audit without digging through raw logs?
3) Any Sev1/Sev2 open bugs tied to the pilot incident (SUP-28479) or “scale to zero” (null predictor) that are not fully closed?

If the answers are clean, I’m fine with GA for bounds (with staged rollout) and predictive staying opt-in.

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
Platform Executive Sponsor
Redwood Inference


From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 3, 2025 at 2:03 PM PDT
Subject: Re: GA Go/No-Go: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode (Sep 3)

Answering (1) + (3) from Infra side:

1) Paging threshold
- We page only when BOTH are true for a sustained window:
  a) bounded_state = “at_max” (or bounded_desired == max) AND
  b) queue_depth above threshold (deployment-level) for > N minutes
- We validated this against pilot traffic ramps; normal ramps where we’re not maxed do not page.
- Non-paging warning exists for “bound-hit rate increasing” (early indicator) routed to #eng-infra.

3) Open bugs
- The scale-to-zero via null predictor is fixed and verified in canary + pilot (PR-48321). No open Sev from that.
- SUP-28479 oscillation: mitigated by cooldown + dampening (PR-48288). We’ve not observed oscillation in last 10 days; leaving a low-priority follow-up to improve forecast confidence display, but not a blocker.

Vanessa


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 3, 2025 at 2:29 PM PDT
Subject: Re: GA Go/No-Go: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode (Sep 3)

On (2) auditability:
- Console shows scaling policy change history per deployment (who/when/what fields changed) and links to the underlying audit event IDs.
- There is also a “scaling decision timeline” view (desired, bounded, reason) for the last 7 days.
- For enterprise audits, Support/CS can export the audit events by deployment and date range. (This is called out in the CS playbook + security FAQ.)

We can answer:
- “Who changed min/max/predictive toggle”
- “What was the effective policy at time T”
- “When we hit max, what signals drove desired vs bounded”

If you’d like, I can send a quick screenshot set, but it’s all referenced in the checklist.

Lauren


From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 3, 2025 at 3:47 PM PDT
Subject: Re: GA Go/No-Go: Dedicated Autoscaling Bounds + Predictive Mode (Sep 3)

Approved to proceed.

Decision:
- GA for customer-configurable bounds (min/max) with staged enablement as described (no behavior change for existing Dedicated unless enabled).
- Predictive mode remains opt-in behind feature flag; treat as “GA available / customer-managed risk” until we have more regional coverage + historical validation.

Launch conditions:
- Keep the “high min requires approval” guardrail.
- Ensure the “min unmet due to shortage” customer messaging is included in docs and Support macro.
- Post-GA monitoring: send me and Neha a 1-week readout (bound-hit rates, max-bound saturation pages, and any customer escalations).

Thanks for driving this.

Priya
